items.title: OpenAI の GPT-6 Astra で「歩ける5km四方の森」を作るなら
items.summary:
OpenAI の GPT-6 Astra で「歩ける5km四方の森」を作るなら
いきなり5kmは頼まず、100m四方から始める。海外で紹介された手順です😳
https://t.co/gPllReJX5d
Astra に100m四方の森を試作してもらう
↓
木の間隔、道、小川、岩、草の量を決めるルールを C++ で書く
↓
川底の石、倒木、シダ、池、ベンチを足す
↓
Unreal Engine の標準キャラクターで歩き、近くで見ておかしい所を直す
↓
100m四方に納得したら、同じルールで5km四方へ広げる
↓
光は Unreal Engine の標準機能に任せ、木登りなどの動きを足す
100m四方 → 5km四方で、面積は2,500倍。
小さな森が作り物っぽく見えるなら、広げても作り物っぽい森が2,500倍の広さになるだけ。
この順番は、ゲーム以外の制作にも使えそうです。
投稿で紹介された手順どおりに進めても、同じ結果になるとは限りません。

items.title: Fable5.2 ロールアウト!!
items.summary:
Fable5.2 ロールアウト!!
すでに全員使える状態です!!
注目すべきベンチスコア等について解説します～
Opus5.5でやった方が良いことも多々あるので公式推奨の使い分けも書きます

■スコアが上がった重要ベンチ
実案件をもとにした成果物づくり（RLI）17.9% → 41.3%  ※1

RLIベンチは実際のフリーランス案件をもとに、AIの成果物が人間の納品物と同等以上と判定された割合で、5.1の約2.3倍です。

つまり、仕事の仕様を渡して丸投げで質の高い成果物を出す割合が大幅に上がったということで、EQや視野の広さ、仕様を満たす要件の詰め方やクオリティを詰める能力が上がった可能性が高いです。

・ハードウェア設計 44.4 → 83.5%
Opus 5.5 は65.3。
公式が一段落のプロンプトから基板・筐体・ソフトまで作り、3つの電子機器を動作させた事例も出しています。AI×ハードウェア革命、く、くる…。

・実務コーディング 32.4% → 49.1%
OSSのメンテナにマージされるコードを書けるかを見るテストで、公開済みモデルでは最高。これはかなり気が効いてないと難しいので、気の利いたコードがかけるようになってる説

■ほかにも大きく伸びたベンチ（5.1 → 5.2）
・ロボット操作 27.6% → 64.9%
　GPT-6 Astra（29.8%）の2倍超
・業務フロー自動化 31.4% → 51.4%
・科学研究のエージェント作業 52.6% → 74.6%
・グラフ読み取り44.8% → 73.4%

■そこまで伸びていないベンチ
・PC操作：89.3%で、Opus 5.5とほぼ同じ
・知的業務：人間が見比べるEloでは1785で、Opus 5.5（1800）のほうがわずかに上。おーん
・AutomationBenchとChartography：5.1から大きく伸びたが、Gemini 4 Carbonとはほぼ横並びか負けです。
・AI研究開発（カーネル最適化・LLM設計）：安全上の理由で、訓練時にあえてOpus 5.5並みに抑えたと公式が明言。
・サイバー・生物：Fableでは大半のタスクが分類器でブロック、この分野をやるならMythos（審査制）が必要。

■価格と速度
- 入力トークンあたり$8/M：$10から低下
- 出力トークンあたり$40/M：$50から低下
- 20%安価
- 最大30%高速化

安くて速くなった？何が起きてる。

■Opus 5.5との使い分け
公式の推奨は「まずOpus 5.5から始め、足りなければFableへ上げる」。

□Opus 5.5がいい時
・日常のコーディングや調べもの、文章作業
・トークン単価が半分なので、量が多い作業
・セキュリティ系の作業

□Fable 5.2がいい時
・Opus 5.5をHigh/Maxにしても届かない難しい問題
・仕様が曖昧な丸投げ、何時間も走る長いエージェント作業
・多数のサブエージェントを指揮する作業
・Opusに作業させ、詰まった時だけFableに相談する「Advisor」構成も公式に案内

スコア見ても
普段使い　→　Opus5.5
丸投げ、大規模改修　→　Fable5.2
って感じはする。意外と主要スコアはOpus5.5からそれほど変わらないものも多いので。
エフォートはHighが一番コスパ良さそう

■Fable 5.5はまだ控えている？
・Azureのカタログに「claude-fable-5-5」の行が一時的に出た（10/13、数日で削除）
・Cursorが「fable-5.5」のモデルIDに対応した（10/17）
・パートナー企業にFable 5.5のチェックポイントが配られた、というリーク（TestingCatalog 10/17、11/1）
みたいなことがあったので、5.2が出て皆「！？」ってなってますね。

上場も控えていることですし、そのタイミングで最強の5.5を出す可能性はあり。

5.2はそのための繋ぎっぽさもあるけど、丸投げ系タスク、長時間タスク、大規模タスクには現時点最強と言って良いスコアなのでバンバン使っていって良さそう

Fableリセットっていう謎チケットも配布されてたので、5.5を待たずに早速私は自分のプロジェクトに使って行くことにするぜ

items.title: Recent Advances in AI Are Creating a ‘Paradigm Shift’ for Robotics | Research UC Berkeley
items.summary:
In recent months, artificial intelligence agents that can reason, plan and use external tools to accomplish multistep tasks have already reshaped computer coding, online shopping, dinner reservations and cyberattacks.

Robotics might be next.

Ken Goldberg, a UC Berkeley roboticist and professor of engineering, said new models make it possible for teams of AI agents to develop robot-control programs, test them in simulated environments and revise the code when something doesn’t work. [...] Then, AI agents generate and connect these skills into a robot program. Using NVIDIA’s Isaac simulation libraries, the agents autonomously rehearse the program across task variations, identify where failures happen and refine the approach before deployment. [...] OpenAI’s recent release of its Astra model made the process even more promising, Goldberg said. His postdoctoral students Eric Kaiyuan Chen and Shuangyu Xie gave Astra access to their simulation interface and a short video of a real robot whose assignment was using a sponge to wipe ink off a metal bar. In less than an hour, the AI tool created and fine-tuned a physics simulation that accurately reproduced the video, including very realistic deformations of the sponge.

items.title: Công nghệ gen tạo động lực đột phá cho ngành nông nghiệp
items.summary:
Giai đoạn 2026-2030, Việt Nam đặt mục tiêu xy dựng ít nhất 5 phòng thí nghiệm trọng điểm và 5 phòng thí nghiệm chuyên ngành hiện đại, tập trung vào công nghệ gen, công nghệ tế bào thực vật và động vật, vi sinh vật, thú y và chẩn đoán dịch bệnh. Mục tiêu đến năm 2035, tầm nhìn đến năm 2045 là làm chủ hoàn toàn công nghệ sinh học thế hệ mới và công nghệ chỉnh sửa gen để tạo ra các sản phẩm thương mại phục vụ thị trường trong nước và xuất khẩu. items.title: Recent Advances in AI Are Creating a ‘Paradigm Shift’ for Robotics | Research UC Berkeley
items.summary:
In recent months, artificial intelligence agents that can reason, plan and use external tools to accomplish multistep tasks have already reshaped computer coding, online shopping, dinner reservations and cyberattacks.

Robotics might be next.

Ken Goldberg, a UC Berkeley roboticist and professor of engineering, said new models make it possible for teams of AI agents to develop robot-control programs, test them in simulated environments and revise the code when something doesn’t work. [...] Then, AI agents generate and connect these skills into a robot program. Using NVIDIA’s Isaac simulation libraries, the agents autonomously rehearse the program across task variations, identify where failures happen and refine the approach before deployment. [...] OpenAI’s recent release of its Astra model made the process even more promising, Goldberg said. His postdoctoral students Eric Kaiyuan Chen and Shuangyu Xie gave Astra access to their simulation interface and a short video of a real robot whose assignment was using a sponge to wipe ink off a metal bar. In less than an hour, the AI tool created and fine-tuned a physics simulation that accurately reproduced the video, including very realistic deformations of the sponge.

items.title: Open source bug fixing using Fable 5.2? 🤔🤔
items.summary:
Open source bug fixing using Fable 5.2? 🤔🤔 

Here is a version you can post as is:

**Got leftover chatbot tokens at the end of the week? Here is one use for them.**

A lot of paid AI subscriptions come with a weekly allowance. Whatever I don't use by the end of the week is gone. So I started asking a simple question: what if the leftover allowance went toward helping strangers?

Here is the idea. Free public software is full of small open bug reports. Many of those reports sit for weeks because the people who maintain the software are volunteers with limited time. Lots of those bugs are small: a typo in a command name or a crash on a weird input or a wrong default value.

So I asked my AI model to do four things:

1. Find open bug reports in public projects that the maintainers labelled as good for beginners.
2. Pick only the small and clear ones. Skip anything that needs a judgment call by the maintainers.
3. Write a short fix and a test for each one.
4. Keep every note short so no volunteer gets buried in a wall of AI text.

In one evening the assistant wrote seven small fixes across six projects. The assistant also skipped eight other bug reports because those eight were unclear. I count the skipping as a feature: a sloppy fix costs a volunteer more time than no fix.

Where I got stuck: the assistant could write the fixes but could not send the fixes to the projects. A safety rule on the AI company's side blocked the assistant from posting to other people's projects under my account and from running the projects' own tests. So right now a human still has to do the sending. I don't know how to do the sending yet and I don't have the energy to learn tonight.

Why I'm posting:

- If you have leftover tokens each week then your leftover tokens could do the same thing.
- If you know how to submit fixes on GitHub then you are the missing piece. One person who knows the sending step could pair with many people who have spare tokens.

items.title: Recent advances in AI are creating a 'paradigm shift' for robotics - Berkeley News
items.summary:
Traditionally, engineers can directly program the software that tells robots how to perceive objects, plan movements and control their actions, a process called model-based robotics. Or, with model-free robotics, they can train robots to learn behaviors from demonstrations through imitation learning. The first approach requires extensive engineering, while the second needs enormous amounts of data and time. [...] Berkeley-based Ambi Robotics, which specializes in logistics and warehouse order fulfillment, applied the new methods earlier this year to analyze parcel sorting data and test updates to robot behavior. Tests showed an increased capacity of over 15,000 packages sorted annually per robot; the change is now deployed across 30% of the company’s U.S. fleet. [...] Ken Goldberg

“Agentic robotics is a fundamental shift in how robots are controlled,” Goldberg said. “Instead of collecting massive amounts of data and hand-tuning every behavior, teams of agents can quickly generate, test and refine robot programs that allow human engineers to interpret how the programs work for fine-tuning and verification.”

items.title: Weekend hack: HackerTube. I was annoyed with YouTube's recommendations so I had Claude filter down 43M comments over 20
items.summary:
Weekend hack: HackerTube. I was annoyed with YouTube's recommendations so I had Claude filter down 43M comments over 20 years of HN to 6,454 videos that keep being recommended. *Significantly* better viewing experience, ~2 hours with Opus 5.5:
https://t.co/JIhXN7OSh1

- Excellent recs without any logins (state is kept in local browser session)
- Thumbnail is a representative frame from middle of the video instead of the super duper A/B test hyper-optimized user uploads
- Underlying data from the comment analysis as one zip file, point your Claude at it and ask for your own version
- HackerTube Longs ✊

A bit more on the process:
I use Claude Code (desktop app for Mac), Opus 5.5 on Medium effort as my default. I only talk to Claude and have it do everything, the only "manual work" I helped with in tandem was in the browser (reminiscent of MenuGen): 1) I had to create some kind of API key from Google Cloud UI to query YouTube for video metadata, 2) I booted up a VPS box for serving and 3) I bought the domain name. Once the box was up I gave Claude the IP and told it update, secure, harden, deploy and optimize the code, and it did the whole thing.

Many awesome projects that would have normally taken weeks/months even can now be few-shotted for breakfast. What else are we not thinking of.
